short.en: Turn JPG images into one PDF.

tools.meta_description: Turn JPG images into one PDF, one photo per page, in your browser. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose one or more JPG images with the file button.
Check that the images are in the order you want, because each image becomes one page in that order.
Press Convert JPG to PDF.
Save the downloaded PDF, which has one image per page.

content.use: JPG to PDF turns photos into a single PDF file, one photo per page. A student photographs handwritten notes and sends them as one PDF to a teacher. A job applicant photographs certificates and attaches one PDF to an application. A shop owner photographs receipts and keeps them as one monthly PDF. Each photo is fitted to an A4 page with a small margin, so nothing is cropped, and the photos stay in the order you selected them. The PDF is built in your browser with jsPDF, so your photos are never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Choose the images in the order you want them to appear, because each image becomes one page in that order. For the sharpest result, use clear photos; a blurry photo stays blurry in the PDF. If a photo is sideways, rotate it on your phone or computer first, because this tool does not rotate images.
content.limit: Only JPG and JPEG images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. Each image is placed on its own page, so you cannot put two images side by side on one page. Very large images are fitted to the page, not kept at full size, and the tool does not rotate images.
content.example: Choosing 4 photos of handwritten notes and pressing Convert JPG to PDF gives one 4-page PDF, with each photo on its own A4 page.
faq: Can I convert a PNG image here?
No. This page only accepts JPG and JPEG images. Use PNG to PDF for PNG images, or Images to PDF if you have a mix of JPG, PNG and WebP images.
How do I set the page order?
Choose the images in the order you want the pages to appear. Each image becomes one page in that order, and there is no reorder step on this page.
What is the downloaded file called?
ak-premium-jpg-to-pdf.pdf. It has one page per image, in the order you selected them, and your original images are not changed.
Can I convert many photos at once?
Yes. Choose as many JPG images as you need, each under 50 MB. Each image becomes one page, so ten photos give a ten-page PDF.

short.en: Turn PNG images into one PDF.

tools.meta_description: Turn PNG images into one PDF, one image per page, in your browser. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose one or more PNG images with the file button.
Check that the images are in the order you want, because each image becomes one page in that order.
Press Convert PNG to PDF.
Save the downloaded PDF, which has one image per page.

content.use: PNG to PDF turns screenshots and pictures into a single PDF file, one image per page. A student screenshots a diagram and sends it as one PDF to a teacher. An office worker screenshots a chart and attaches one PDF to a report. A designer screenshots a mockup and shares one PDF with a client. Each image is fitted to an A4 page with a small margin, so nothing is cropped, and the images stay in the order you selected them. The PDF is built in your browser with jsPDF, so your images are never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Choose the images in the order you want them to appear, because each image becomes one page in that order. PNG images keep sharp edges, so they suit screenshots and diagrams. If an image is sideways, rotate it on your phone or computer first, because this tool does not rotate images.
content.limit: Only PNG images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. Each image is placed on its own page, so you cannot put two images side by side on one page. Very large images are fitted to the page, not kept at full size, and the tool does not rotate images.
content.example: Choosing 3 screenshots of a chart and pressing Convert PNG to PDF gives one 3-page PDF, with each screenshot on its own A4 page.
faq: Can I convert a JPG image here?
No. This page only accepts PNG images. Use JPG to PDF for JPG images, or Images to PDF if you have a mix of JPG, PNG and WebP images.
Does the PDF keep full image quality?
No. Each image is fitted to an A4 page, so a very large image is scaled down. The result is a clean, readable PDF, not a full-resolution archive of your images.
What file do I get after converting?
You download one PDF named ak-premium-png-to-pdf.pdf. It has one page per image, in the order you selected them, and your original images are not changed.
Can I convert many screenshots at once?
Yes. Choose as many PNG images as you need, each under 50 MB. Each image becomes one page, so ten screenshots give a ten-page PDF.

short.en: Render PDF pages as JPG images.

tools.meta_description: Render PDF pages as JPG images, with a download link per page and one ZIP file. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Press Convert PDF to JPG and wait for the status message to say it is done.
Download each page JPG from the links shown, such as Download page 2 JPG.
Or download the whole set at once as one ZIP file named ak-premium-pages.zip.

content.use: PDF to JPG turns every page of a PDF into a JPG picture, so you can share a single page in a chat, add it to a slide or post it online. A teacher turns one page of a worksheet into a JPG to share in a class group. A student turns a diagram page into a JPG to paste into an assignment. A shop owner turns a price page into a JPG for a social media post. Each page is rendered at one and a half times its normal size for a sharp picture. After the conversion, you get a download link for each page and one ZIP file with all the pages together.
content.tip: If you only need one page, download just that page's JPG link instead of the whole ZIP. JPG files are smaller than PNG, so they suit sharing in chats. Large PDFs take a while because every page is rendered in your browser, so wait for the status message to say it is done.
content.limit: Each page becomes a separate JPG, so a 50-page PDF gives 50 pictures and one ZIP. The JPGs are pictures of the pages, not editable text. A scanned PDF renders as a picture of the scan, which is fine, but a very large PDF may be slow or run out of browser memory.
content.example: Converting a 3-page worksheet gives three JPG links, page 1, page 2 and page 3, plus a ZIP file with all three JPGs inside.
faq: Can I download just one page?
Yes. After the conversion, each page has its own link, such as Download page 2 JPG. Press the link for the page you need. The ZIP is only for downloading all pages at once.
What size are the JPG images?
Each page is rendered at one and a half times its normal size, so the pictures are sharp enough to share or print. They are not full-resolution scans.
Can I get PNG images instead of JPG?
Yes. Use PDF to PNG for PNG images. This page only makes JPG images, which are smaller and suit sharing in chats.
Why is a long PDF slow to convert?
Every page is drawn in your browser one by one. A long PDF with many pages takes longer, and a very large file may run out of memory. Try a smaller file if it stops.

short.en: Render PDF pages as PNG images.

tools.meta_description: Render PDF pages as PNG images, with a download link per page and one ZIP file. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Press Convert PDF to PNG and wait for the status message to say it is done.
Download each page PNG from the links shown, such as Download page 2 PNG.

content.use: PDF to PNG turns every page of a PDF into a PNG picture, which keeps sharp edges and is easy to edit afterwards. A teacher turns a worksheet page into a PNG to crop and reuse in a new handout. A student turns a diagram page into a PNG to label it in an image editor. A designer turns a layout page into a PNG to check the spacing closely. Each page is rendered at one and a half times its normal size, so text stays crisp. After the conversion, you get a download link for each page and one ZIP file with all the pages together.
content.tip: If you only need one page, download just that page's PNG link instead of the whole ZIP. PNG keeps text sharp, so it suits diagrams and pages you want to edit. Large PDFs take a while because every page is rendered in your browser, so wait for the status message to say it is done.
content.limit: Each page becomes a separate PNG, so a 50-page PDF gives 50 pictures and one ZIP. The PNGs are pictures of the pages, not editable text. A scanned PDF renders as a picture of the scan, which is fine, but a very large PDF may be slow or run out of browser memory.
content.example: Converting a 3-page worksheet gives three PNG links, page 1, page 2 and page 3, plus a ZIP file with all three PNGs inside.
faq: How do I save a single page?
After the conversion, each page has its own link, such as Download page 2 PNG. Press the link for the page you need. The ZIP is only for downloading all pages at once.
Are the PNG images full size?
No. Each page is rendered at one and a half times its normal size, so the pictures are sharp enough to share or print. They are not full-resolution scans.
Can I choose JPG output here?
No. This page only makes PNG images, which keep text sharper and suit editing. Use PDF to JPG for JPG images.
What if my PDF is very large?
Every page is drawn in your browser one by one, so a long PDF takes longer. A very large file may run out of memory. Try a smaller file if the conversion stops.

short.en: Turn an HTML file into a PDF.

tools.meta_description: Turn a saved HTML file into a PDF in your browser. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose an HTML file with the file button. The file must end in .html or .htm.
Press Convert HTML to PDF.
Wait for the status message to say the PDF is downloaded.
Open the PDF to check the text, because HTML tags and formatting are not kept.

content.use: HTML to PDF turns a saved web page file into a PDF, which is handy when you have a page saved on your computer and need it as a document. A student saves a course page as an HTML file and turns it into a PDF to read offline. An office worker saves a notice from a website and turns it into a PDF to attach to an email. A shop owner saves a price page and turns it into a PDF to print. The HTML tags are stripped out, so the result is plain text in a simple 12-point font, flowing across pages as needed. Nothing is uploaded; the PDF is built in your browser.
content.tip: Save the web page as an HTML file first, then choose it here. Check the PDF after converting, because the tool strips HTML tags and extra spaces. For a clean result, use a simple page rather than one full of menus and adverts.
content.limit: HTML tags are stripped and formatting is not kept. The PDF is plain 12-point text only, with no bold, headings, images or tables. Very long pages flow across pages automatically, but you cannot choose the font, size or page layout. A page that is mostly images gives a PDF with little or no text.
content.example: Choosing a saved notice page and pressing Convert HTML to PDF downloads ak-premium-html-to-pdf.pdf with the page's words as plain text on one page.
faq: Will my page look the same in the PDF?
No. All HTML tags are stripped out and the text becomes plain 12-point text. Use it for simple pages, not for formatted web pages.
What happens to very long pages?
The text flows across pages automatically. The tool adds pages as needed, so a long page becomes a multi-page PDF.
Can I convert a web page by its address?
No. You must save the page as an HTML file on your device first, then choose that file here. The tool does not fetch pages from the internet.
Is my HTML file uploaded anywhere?
No. The PDF is built in your browser with jsPDF, so the file never leaves your device. No account is needed and nothing is sent to a server.

short.en: Save the images inside a PDF as PNG files.

tools.meta_description: Save the images embedded in a PDF as PNG files, one link per image and one ZIP file. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Press Extract Images and wait for the status message to say it is done.
Download each image PNG from the links shown, such as Download ak-premium-image-1-1.png.
Or download all the images at once as one ZIP file named ak-premium-images.zip.

content.use: Extract Images from PDF saves the pictures that are embedded inside a PDF as separate PNG files, so you can reuse them. A teacher takes a diagram out of a PDF handout to use in a new worksheet. A student saves a chart from a PDF report to paste into an assignment. A shop owner saves a product photo from a PDF catalogue to post online. Each image is saved at its original size as a PNG, with its page number in the file name. The images are read in your browser, so your PDF is never uploaded anywhere.
content.tip: If you only need one image, download just its PNG link instead of the whole ZIP. The file name shows the page number, so ak-premium-image-2-1.png is the first image on page 2. Large PDFs take a while because every page is read in your browser, so wait for the status message to say it is done.
content.limit: Only embedded image objects are found. Tiny inline images, vector drawings and page backgrounds are not extracted, so a PDF made only of shapes may give no images. Some images may be skipped if their format cannot be read. The extracted PNGs are the embedded pictures, not the whole page.
content.example: Extracting images from a 5-page catalogue with 2 photos on page 1 and 1 chart on page 3 gives 3 PNG links and a ZIP file with all 3 images inside.
faq: What images does this tool find?
It finds pictures embedded inside the PDF, such as photos and charts. It does not find vector drawings, page backgrounds or tiny inline images, so some PDFs give no images at all.
Are the images saved at full size?
Yes. Each image is saved at the size it is stored in the PDF. The PNG is the embedded picture itself, not a screenshot of the page.
Can I download just one image?
Yes. After the extraction, each image has its own link, such as Download ak-premium-image-1-1.png. Press the link for the image you need. The ZIP is only for downloading all images at once.
Why did my PDF give no images?
The PDF may have no embedded pictures. A text-only PDF, or one made of vector shapes and backgrounds, has nothing to extract. Try PDF to Images if you need a picture of the whole page.

title.en: Add Header and Footer to PDF

short.en: Stamp header and footer text on every page.

tools.meta_description: Stamp the same header and footer text on every page of a PDF, in your browser. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Type the header text in the Header text field, or leave it blank if you only want a footer.
Type the footer text in the Footer text field, or leave it blank if you only want a header.
Press Add Header & Footer.
Save the downloaded PDF, which has the header and footer on every page.

content.use: Add Header and Footer to PDF stamps the same header and footer text on every page of a PDF, which is handy when a document needs a title, a page note or a company name on each page. A teacher adds a class name at the top and a date at the bottom of a handout. An office worker adds a project name at the top and a confidentiality note at the bottom of a report. A shop owner adds a shop name at the top and a phone number at the bottom of a price list. The text is stamped in a small grey font near the top and bottom edges, and the original pages are not changed.
content.tip: Keep the header and footer short, under about 90 characters each, so the text fits on the page. Use the header for a title or project name and the footer for a date or page note. You can fill in only one of the two fields if you need just a header or just a footer.
content.limit: The header and footer are stamped in a fixed small grey font near the top and bottom edges, and you cannot choose the font, size or colour. Very long text is shrunk to fit, and text longer than the page width is cut off. The stamp is added to every page, so you cannot skip a page.
content.example: Adding the header Spring Term 2026 and the footer Page 1 of 10 to a 4-page handout gives a 4-page PDF with the header at the top and the footer at the bottom of every page.
faq: Can I add only a header?
Yes. Fill in the Header text field and leave the Footer text field blank. The tool adds only the header, and the footer is skipped on every page.
Can I add only a footer?
Yes. Fill in the Footer text field and leave the Header text field blank. The tool adds only the footer, and the header is skipped on every page.
Can I change the font or colour?
No. The header and footer use a fixed small grey Helvetica font. You cannot choose the font, size or colour on this page.
Does the stamp cover my page text?
It can, if your page text runs to the very top or bottom edge. The header sits near the top and the footer near the bottom, so pages with wide margins work best.

short.en: Flatten form fields and annotations in a PDF.

tools.meta_description: Flatten a PDF so form fields become permanent text and annotations are removed. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Press Flatten PDF and wait for the status message to say it is done.
Save the downloaded PDF named ak-premium-flattened.pdf.
Open the PDF to check that the form answers are now part of the page, because flattening cannot be undone.

content.use: Flatten PDF turns form fields and annotations in a PDF into permanent page content, so the filled-in answers and notes can no longer be changed or removed. A student flattens a filled application form before sending it, so the answers cannot be edited by mistake. An office worker flattens a signed form so the signature stays as it is. A shop owner flattens a price list with notes so the notes print exactly as shown. Form fields become plain text on the page, and annotations such as comments and links are removed. The flattened PDF looks the same, but nothing in it can be edited as a form any more.
content.tip: Keep a copy of the original PDF before you flatten it, because flattening cannot be undone. Flatten a form only after every field is filled in, because empty fields become blank text. Check the flattened PDF before you send it, to make sure every answer is still readable.
content.limit: Flattening cannot be undone, so keep a copy of the original. Form fields become plain text and can no longer be edited or filled in. Annotations such as comments, highlights and links are removed. A password-protected PDF must be unlocked first.
content.example: Flattening a 2-page application form with 10 filled fields gives a 2-page PDF where the answers are now part of the page and cannot be changed.
faq: What does flattening a PDF do?
It turns form fields into permanent text on the page and removes annotations. The PDF looks the same, but the fields can no longer be edited or filled in.
Can I undo flattening?
No. Flattening is permanent. Keep a copy of the original PDF before you flatten it, because the form fields cannot be restored afterwards.
Does flattening change how the PDF looks?
No. The filled-in answers stay where they were, as plain text on the page. Only the ability to edit them is gone, and annotations such as comments are removed.
Can I flatten a protected PDF?
No. A password-protected PDF must be unlocked first. Use Unlock PDF with the password, then flatten the unlocked file. The unlocked file is a normal PDF that this tool can open.

short.en: View and edit a PDF's title, author and more.

tools.meta_description: View and edit a PDF's title, author, subject and keywords, in your browser. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Read the current title, author, subject and keywords shown under Current metadata, and check the fields are filled in with them.
Change the Title, Author, Subject or Keywords fields to the values you want.
Press Update Metadata.
Save the downloaded PDF, which has the new metadata and the same pages.

content.use: PDF Metadata Editor shows and changes the hidden details of a PDF, such as its title, author, subject and keywords. A student sets the title and author of an assignment PDF so it shows the right name in a reader. An office worker sets the subject of a report PDF so it is easy to find later. A shop owner sets keywords on a price list PDF so it turns up in a search. The metadata is the text a PDF reader shows in the document properties, and it does not change the pages themselves. The edited PDF is saved with the same pages and layout, only the details are new.
content.tip: Fill in the title and author first, because those are the details most readers show. Use keywords that describe the document, separated by commas, so it is easy to find later. Leave a field blank if you want that detail removed from the PDF.
content.limit: Only the title, author, subject and keywords can be changed. The producer, creator and dates are not edited by this tool. A password-protected PDF must be unlocked first. Some PDF readers may still show old details if they cached the file.
content.example: Setting the title to Spring Term Report, the author to Ayesha Khan and the keywords to term report, spring 2026 on a 6-page PDF gives a 6-page PDF with those details in its properties.
faq: What is PDF metadata?
It is the hidden detail stored in a PDF, such as its title, author, subject and keywords. A PDF reader shows it in the document properties, and search tools can use it to find the file.
Does editing metadata change my pages?
No. The pages, text and layout stay exactly the same. Only the title, author, subject and keywords stored in the file are changed.
Can I remove a detail?
Yes. Leave that field blank and press Update Metadata. The blank detail is removed from the PDF, and the other details are kept.
Can I edit a protected PDF?
No. A password-protected PDF must be unlocked first. Use Unlock PDF with the password, then edit the metadata of the unlocked file.

short.en: Scale every page to A4, Letter or Legal.

tools.meta_description: Scale every page of a PDF to A4, Letter or Legal, in your browser. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Pick a page size from the Page size list: A4, Letter or Legal.
Press Resize Pages.
Save the downloaded PDF, which has every page at the size you picked.

content.use: Resize PDF Page Size scales every page of a PDF to A4, Letter or Legal, which is handy when a PDF was made for a different paper size and needs to print cleanly. A student resizes a US Letter assignment to A4 so it prints correctly on local paper. An office worker resizes an A4 report to Letter for a client in the United States. A shop owner resizes a Legal-size price list to A4 for a local printer. Each page is scaled to fit the new size, keeping its shape, and centred on the page. The text and pictures are scaled with the page, so nothing is cropped.
content.tip: Pick the size your printer uses before you resize, because A4 is the usual size in Pakistan and Letter is the usual size in the United States. If the original page is a very different shape, the scaled page has small margins on two sides. Check the resized PDF before you print it.
content.limit: Each page is scaled to fit the new size, keeping its shape, so a page of a very different shape has small margins on two sides. Form fields and links are not carried over to the resized pages. A password-protected PDF must be unlocked first.
content.example: Resizing a 3-page US Letter assignment to A4 gives a 3-page PDF at A4 size (595 by 842 points), with each page scaled to fit and centred.
faq: What sizes can I choose?
A4, Letter and Legal. A4 is 595 by 842 points, Letter is 612 by 792 points, and Legal is 612 by 1008 points. Pick the size your printer uses.
Does resizing crop my pages?
No. Each page is scaled to fit the new size, keeping its shape, and centred on the page. Nothing is cropped, but a page of a very different shape has small margins on two sides.
Does resizing change my text?
No. The text and pictures are scaled with the page, so they stay in the same place relative to each other. Only the page size and the scale change.
Can I resize a protected PDF?
No. A password-protected PDF must be unlocked first. Use Unlock PDF with the password, then resize the unlocked file. The unlocked file is a normal PDF that this tool can open.

short.en: Turn PNG images into JPG.

tools.meta_description: Turn PNG images into JPG in your browser, free and private. Transparent parts become white.
steps: Choose a PNG image with the file button.
Check the file name shown under the button is the right image.
Press Convert PNG to JPG.
Save the downloaded JPG, which has the same width and height as the PNG.

content.use: PNG to JPG turns a PNG picture into a JPG file, keeping the same width and height. A student turns a PNG screenshot into a JPG to upload to a portal that only takes JPG files. A shop owner turns product PNGs into JPGs so the online shop loads faster. An office worker turns a PNG chart into a JPG to paste into a report. JPG files are much smaller than PNG files, so they are easier to send and upload. The picture is converted in your browser with the canvas, so your image is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use PNG to JPG when you need a smaller file for upload or sharing. If your PNG has transparency, remember the see-through parts become white in JPG, so convert to PNG instead if you need to keep transparency. For the sharpest result, start from a clear PNG; a blurry picture stays blurry after conversion.
content.limit: Only PNG images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. JPG has no transparency, so see-through parts of the PNG become white. The picture keeps its original width and height; this tool does not resize it.
content.example: Converting a 1200 by 800 PNG screenshot gives a 1200 by 800 JPG file that is much smaller and ready to upload.
faq: What happens to transparency in JPG?
It becomes white. JPG has no transparency, so the see-through parts of your PNG become white. Convert to PNG or WebP instead if you need to keep the transparency.
Does the JPG keep the same size?
Yes. The width and height stay exactly the same as the PNG. Only the file format changes. Use Image Resizer if you also need a different size.
Can I convert several PNG images at once?
No. This page converts one PNG image at a time. Choose one image, press Convert PNG to JPG, save the result, then choose the next image.
What name does the JPG download with?
ak-premium-png-to-jpg.jpg. It has the same width and height as your PNG, and your original PNG file is not changed in any way.

short.en: Turn JPG images into PNG.

tools.meta_description: Turn JPG images into PNG in your browser, free and private. The picture keeps its size.
steps: Choose a JPG image with the file button.
Check the file name shown under the button is the right image.
Press Convert JPG to PNG.
Save the downloaded PNG, which has the same width and height as the JPG.

content.use: JPG to PNG turns a JPG photo into a PNG file, keeping the same width and height. A designer turns a JPG photo into PNG to edit it in a program that needs PNG. content.limit: Only JPG and JPEG images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. PNG is lossless, so the file is usually larger than the JPG. The picture keeps its original width and height; this tool does not resize it.
content.example: Converting a 1200 by 800 JPG photo gives a 1200 by 800 PNG file with the same picture and no JPG smudges.
faq: Will the PNG be better quality than the JPG?
No. PNG is lossless, but it cannot add detail that the JPG already lost. The PNG keeps exactly the detail in your JPG, without adding new JPG smudges.
Why is the PNG file larger?
PNG is lossless, so it stores every pixel exactly. JPG throws away detail to make a smaller file. The PNG keeps all the detail, so it is usually larger than the same picture as a JPG.
Can I convert several JPG images at once?

What name does the PNG download with?
ak-premium-jpg-to-png.png. It has the same width and height as your JPG, and your original JPG file is not changed in any way.

content.tip: Use WebP to JPG when a site or program refuses WebP files. If your WebP has transparency, the see-through parts become white in JPG, so convert to PNG instead to keep transparency. WebP files are usually small, so the JPG may be larger than the WebP.
content.limit: Only WebP images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. JPG has no transparency, so see-through parts of the WebP become white. The picture keeps its original width and height; this tool does not resize it.
content.example: Converting a 1200 by 800 WebP screenshot gives a 1200 by 800 JPG file that uploads to a portal that only accepts JPG.
faq: Why do some sites not accept WebP?
WebP is newer than JPG, so some portals, printers and old programs only accept JPG or PNG. Converting to JPG gives you a file those sites accept, with the same picture.
Does the JPG lose quality?
A little. JPG throws away some detail to make a smaller file, while WebP keeps more. The picture looks the same at normal size, but fine detail can soften slightly.
Can I convert several WebP images at once?
No. This page converts one WebP image at a time. Choose one image, press Convert WebP to JPG, save the result, then choose the next image.
Where does the JPG download go?
To your browser download folder, as ak-premium-webp-to-jpg.jpg. It has the same width and height as your WebP, and your original WebP file is not changed.

PNG is lossless, so it stores every pixel exactly. WebP throws away some detail to make a smaller file. The PNG keeps all the detail, so it is usually larger than the same picture as a WebP.

Where is the downloaded PNG saved?
In your browser download folder, as ak-premium-webp-to-png.png. It has the same width and height as your WebP, and your original WebP file is not changed.

short.en: Turn JPG images into WebP.

content.example: Converting a 1200 by 800 JPG photo gives a 1200 by 800 WebP file that is much smaller and loads faster on a website.
faq: How much smaller is the WebP file?

Usually much smaller than the JPG, often by a third or more, because WebP compresses photos better. The exact saving depends on the picture; a photo with lots of detail saves less than a plain screenshot.
Can old programs open WebP?
Most modern browsers open WebP, but some old photo programs and printers do not. If you are not sure, keep the JPG as well, or convert back with WebP to JPG.
Does WebP lose quality?

ak-premium-jpg-to-webp.webp. It has the same width and height as your JPG, and your original JPG file is not changed in any way.

short.en: Turn SVG files into PNG images.

tools.meta_description: Turn SVG files into PNG images in your browser, free and private. Choose the output width.
steps: Choose an SVG file with the file button.
Enter the output width in pixels in the Width box, or leave 1024.
Press Convert SVG to PNG.
Save the downloaded PNG, which has the width you entered and the same shape as the SVG.

content.use: SVG to PNG turns a vector SVG file into a PNG picture at the width you choose. A designer turns a logo SVG into a PNG to use it in a document or a presentation that does not take SVG. A shop owner turns an SVG icon into a PNG to put it on a website. A student turns an SVG diagram into a PNG to paste it into an assignment. The PNG keeps the shape of the SVG, and a bigger width gives a sharper picture. The conversion runs in your browser, so your file is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use a bigger width for a sharper PNG, because the SVG is drawn fresh at that size. Leave the width at 1024 for most uses. If the PNG comes out blank, your SVG may use an external image or font that the browser cannot load here.
content.limit: Only SVG files are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. The PNG keeps the SVG shape, but text in the SVG uses your browser fonts, so it can look different from the original program. SVGs that link to external images or fonts cannot be drawn and give an error.
content.example: Converting a logo SVG at width 1024 gives a PNG that is 1024 pixels wide, with the same shape as the logo, ready to paste into a document.
faq: Why is my PNG blank or missing parts?
Your SVG probably links to an external image or font that the browser cannot load here. Save the SVG with its images and fonts embedded, or use a plain SVG with shapes and text only.
What width should I enter?
1024 pixels works for most uses. Enter a bigger width, such as 2048, for a sharper picture or a large print. The height follows the SVG shape automatically.
Does the PNG keep transparency?
Yes. If your SVG has see-through parts, the PNG keeps them see-through. The PNG is saved with transparency, so you can place it on any background.
Can I convert an SVG with text in it?
Yes, but the text is drawn with your browser fonts, so it can look different from the original program. For an exact match, turn the text into shapes in your drawing program first.

short.en: Crop an image to the part you need.

tools.meta_description: Crop an image in your browser, free and private. Drag to choose the area, then download a PNG.
steps: Choose a JPG, PNG or WebP image with the file button.
Drag on the preview to draw the rectangle you want to keep.
Fine-tune the rectangle with the X, Y, Width and Height boxes.
Press Crop Image.
Save the downloaded PNG, which holds only the rectangle you chose.

content.use: Image Cropper cuts a picture down to the part you want, and saves it as a PNG. A student crops a screenshot to keep only one diagram for an assignment. A shop owner crops a product photo to remove the messy background around it. A job applicant crops a photo to keep only their face for a profile picture. You drag a rectangle on the preview, and the numbers in the X, Y, Width and Height boxes show exactly which part is kept. The crop runs in your browser with the canvas, so your photo is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Drag on the preview to draw the rectangle, then use the X, Y, Width and Height boxes to set it exactly. Keep the rectangle inside the picture; numbers that go past the edge are pulled back inside. The output is always PNG, which keeps the picture sharp.
content.limit: JPG, PNG and WebP images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. The output is always a PNG file, even if you cropped a JPG. The crop keeps only the rectangle you drew; the rest of the picture is thrown away, so keep a copy of the original.
content.example: Cropping a 1200 by 800 screenshot to a 600 by 400 rectangle gives a 600 by 400 PNG with only the diagram you selected.
faq: How do I choose the crop area?
Drag on the preview with your mouse or finger to draw a rectangle. The X, Y, Width and Height boxes show the rectangle in pixels, and you can type new numbers there to set it exactly.
Why is the output a PNG file?
PNG is lossless, so the cropped picture keeps all its detail. Even if you cropped a JPG, the result is a PNG. Use Image Converter afterwards if you need a JPG.
Can I crop to an exact size?
Yes. Type the exact Width and Height in pixels in the boxes, and set X and Y to place the rectangle. Press Crop Image and the PNG will have exactly that width and height.
Can I undo a crop?
No. The crop throws away everything outside the rectangle. Keep a copy of the original picture, or choose the same image again and draw a new rectangle.

short.en: Rotate or flip an image in your browser.

tools.meta_description: Rotate or flip an image in your browser, free and private. Turn it left or right, or mirror it.
steps: Choose a JPG, PNG or WebP image with the file button.
Press Rotate Left or Rotate Right to turn the picture, or Flip Horizontal or Flip Vertical to mirror it.
Pick the output format, PNG or JPEG, in the Output format box.
Press Download Image.
Save the downloaded picture, which has the rotation and flip you applied.

content.use: Rotate and Flip Image turns a picture left or right, or mirrors it, without changing anything else. A student rotates a sideways photo of handwritten notes so it reads the right way up. A shop owner flips a product photo to match the layout of a web page. A job applicant rotates a scanned certificate that came out sideways. Each press of Rotate Left or Rotate Right turns the picture by 90 degrees, and Flip Horizontal or Flip Vertical mirrors it. The changes run in your browser with the canvas, so your photo is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Press Rotate Right once for a photo that is sideways clockwise, or three times for one that is sideways the other way. Flip Horizontal mirrors a picture left to right, which is useful for a selfie that looks reversed. Choose JPEG for photos and PNG if you need transparency.
content.limit: JPG, PNG and WebP images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. Rotating by 90 degrees swaps the width and height. Saving as JPEG flattens transparency onto a white background, because JPG has no transparency.
content.example: Rotating a 800 by 1200 sideways photo once to the right gives a 1200 by 800 photo that reads the right way up.
faq: How many times do I press Rotate Right?
Once for a photo that is sideways clockwise, twice to turn it upside down, and three times for a photo that is sideways the other way. Each press turns the picture by 90 degrees.
What is the difference between flip and rotate?
Rotate turns the picture around, so the top becomes a side. Flip mirrors it, so the left and right swap but the top stays on top. A flipped photo is a mirror image, not a rotated one.
Why is the width and height swapped?

Rotating by 90 degrees turns the picture on its side, so the old width becomes the new height and the old height becomes the new width. Rotating twice, by 180 degrees, keeps the width and height the same.
Which output format should I pick?
Pick JPEG for photos, because it makes smaller files. Pick PNG if your picture has transparency or sharp text, because PNG keeps both exactly. JPEG turns see-through parts white.

short.en: Make a passport photo at the right size.

tools.meta_description: Make a passport photo at the right size for Pakistan, India, USA, UK, EU, UAE or Canada, in your browser.
steps: Choose a clear front-facing photo with the file button.
Pick your country in the Country box, such as Pakistan, USA or Canada.
Check the size shown under the Country box matches your form.
Press Make Passport Photo.
Save the downloaded JPG, which has the exact size for that country.

content.use: Passport Photo Maker cuts your photo to the exact passport size for your country and saves it as a JPG. Pakistan, UK, EU and UAE use 35 by 45 mm, which is 413 by 531 pixels. India and the USA use 2 by 2 inches, which is 600 by 600 pixels. Canada uses 50 by 70 mm, which is 591 by 827 pixels. The tool crops the centre of your photo to the right shape and resizes it to the exact pixels, so you can print it or upload it to a form. The photo is made in your browser, so your picture is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use a clear photo taken against a plain light background, with your face in the centre and looking at the camera. The tool crops the centre, so keep your face in the middle of the photo. Check the size on your official form before you print or submit, because rules change.
content.limit: JPG, PNG and WebP photos are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. The tool only sets the size and shape; it cannot fix a blurry photo, bad light or a wrong background, and it cannot guarantee a form will accept the photo. Sizes follow the common official rules, but always check your form, because some visas use a different size.
content.example: Choosing a photo and picking Pakistan gives a 413 by 531 pixel JPG, which is 35 by 45 mm, ready to print or upload.
faq: What size is a Pakistan passport photo?
35 by 45 mm, which is 413 by 531 pixels. Pick Pakistan in the Country box and the tool makes a JPG at exactly that size.
What size is a USA passport photo?
2 by 2 inches, which is 51 by 51 mm or 600 by 600 pixels. Pick USA in the Country box and the tool makes a square JPG at exactly that size.
Why is my face cut off?
The tool crops the centre of your photo to the passport shape. Use a photo with your face in the centre and some space around it, so the crop keeps your whole face.
Will my form accept this photo?
The tool sets the exact size for the country you pick, but acceptance also depends on light, background, expression and the form rules. Check the official photo rules on your form before you submit.

short.en: Convert length, weight, temperature, pressure and more.

tools.meta_description: Convert length, weight, temperature, area, volume, speed, data, time, energy, pressure, power, fuel economy and cooking units in your browser.
steps: Choose the kind of unit in the 'Unit type' list, such as Length, Pressure, Energy, Power, Fuel or Cooking.
Type the number in the 'Value' box. The result updates as you type, and shows every unit of that kind at once.
Choose the unit you have in the 'From' list and the unit you want in the 'To' list, or press Swap to reverse them.
In Cooking mode, pick an ingredient to change grams into cups, or cups into grams.

content.use: Unit Converter changes a measurement from one unit to another in your browser. A student changes 5 kilometres into metres for homework. A driver checks fuel use in miles per gallon against litres per 100 km. A cook changes 250 grams of flour into cups. Typing a value shows every unit of that kind at once, so 5 km shows metres, miles and feet together. Common pairs are one tap away, and recent conversions are remembered in this browser.
content.tip: In Cooking mode, pick the ingredient first: one cup of flour weighs about 120 grams but one cup of sugar weighs about 200 grams, so the answer changes. For fuel, remember that a smaller litres-per-100-km number means better economy, while a bigger miles-per-gallon number does. Press Swap to reverse a conversion instead of retyping it.
content.limit: Cooking cup weights are estimates from common density tables, not exact measurements, and are labelled as estimates.
